title: model-right-sizer Agent Output-Schema Prescription
description: Strict output contract for the model-right-sizer agent's per-agent schema-prescription lever (the 'Agent-to-agent message-schema design' lever, scoped to one agent-to-controller seam instead of a whole flow's blueprint). The agent emits exactly one JSON object conforming to this schema instead of prose. See agent-schema.example.json for a worked instance, and agent-schema-families.md for the family catalogue `family.id` is picked from. additionalProperties is false at every level on purpose -- an agent cannot reintroduce free-form fields.

schema_version.description: Bump alongside this file when the shape changes.

task_type.description: The target agent's own task-type identifier, stamped into its schema block (e.g. 'log_triage', 'code_review').

in_fields.description: The typed brief the target agent receives. Anything large must arrive as a reference (path, id, state key), never inlined -- see current_shape/exclude.

out_fields.description: The typed payload the target agent hands its controller. This is the whole point of the prescription: name every field the controller actually consumes, and nothing else.

prose_field.description: The ONE bounded prose slot this family allows, if any. null means the family (e.g. watch-report, candidate-set) structurally carries no prose slot -- that is a valid, often deliberate, answer, not an omission.

exclude.description: This agent's exclusion list, beyond the universal list in agent-schema-families.md -- what this handoff must NOT carry (e.g. 'raw log lines', 'the full diff body', 'stack traces').

stamp_markdown.description: The literal, ready-to-insert '## Agent-to-agent schema' block (with its begin/end marker comments) for the target agent's file. Must restate family/task_type/in/out/exclude as prose -- never just a pointer to the other fields on this object.

rationale.description: Why this family and this field set -- not just 'because the catalogue has it'.

file_ref.description: Path to the target agent's .md file, or null if it doesn't exist as a file yet (a schema prescribed ahead of writing the agent).

name.description: The orchestrator, skill, or parent agent that dispatches the target agent and consumes its reply.

needs.description: What the controller actually acts on from the reply -- the thing the whole prescription is sized against.

kind.description: none_yet = the target agent doesn't exist as a file yet, so there is nothing to compare against; the prescription is the agent's first schema, not a tightening of an existing one.

note.description: One or two clauses on what today's shape actually looks like (or would default to).

id.description: A family id from the chosen catalogue (e.g. 'scored-review'), or a newly-coined id when none fits.

is_new_family.description: True only when no existing family in the chosen catalogue fits this seam's shape.

catalogue_source.description: repo_catalogue = the target repo already has its own family catalogue and this pick came from there; plugin_portable_catalogue = agent-schema-families.md, this plugin's fallback.

shape_summary.description: One clause naming the family's shape, e.g. 'scorecard + findings + leave_alone'.

baseline.description: What the target agent would otherwise hand its controller, e.g. 'unscoped prose reply, ~400-800 words typical'.

prescribed.description: The size/shape of the prescribed payload, e.g. '6 typed fields + one <=150-word prose slot'.

rationale.description: Why the prescribed shape is smaller and still sufficient for the controller's stated needs.
